title: Interactive column grips with keyboard-first microinteractions for large virtualized tables
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: design an accessible, performant column-resize affordance ("grip") that works across keyboard, mouse, and touch for deeply virtualized tables and cooperates with density-compression modes and column auto-layout tokens. Background: current table resize uses a thin hit target and requires mouse-only pixel-precise drags; this is fragile under virtualization (handles repaint/reflow), has poor keyboard support, and is inconsistent with tokens for focus / motion. Constraints: must avoid full table reflows during continuous drag; must support very wide tables with tens of columns; must respect density mode compression rules and per-column priority; must work inside VDOM/virtualization boundaries without forcing full rerender.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a dedicated interactive grip UI that sits in the column header gutter. The grip has a larger invisible hit target (tokenized hitSize), visible microinteraction (tokenized focus ring, hover halo), and a detachable ghost preview layer for live width preview.
- Keyboard-first behavior: when header receives focus, pressing (or long-pressing on touch) a grip key (Enter/Space) toggles resize mode; ArrowLeft/ArrowRight nudge width by small tokenized increments; Shift+Arrow nudges by larger steps; double-press auto-fit to content. Escape cancels. Tab order remains unchanged (grip focus separate from cell focus).
- Mouse/touch behavior: pointerdown begins a resize preview; we use a composition model that updates a lightweight preview layer (CSS transform) while accumulating width deltas into a debounced commit to the column width state (200ms debounce). This prevents continuous writes through the virtualization layer but keeps the visual feedback immediate.
- Accessibility: announce width changes to a polite ARIA live region ("Column {name} width {px}"), expose pointerless controls for screen-reader users (plus/minus buttons reachable from header toolbar), and ensure focus and drag operations are announced. Provide a 4th-level contrast visible focus ring token.
- Density and token integration: resizing respects density token ranges (compact|minWidth, default|minWidth, spacious|minWidth). When a resize would violate density constraints, the UI shows a subtle compression affordance and an inline tooltip explaining effects ("resizing will compress column content in compact density").
- Performance: use a renderer-friendly implementation: preview uses transform on a separate overlay element; commits use a single state update that the virtualization layer picks up. For large drag sequences we'll only write final width plus a single intermediate commit every 200ms.

Design deliverables: high-fidelity Figma frames (mouse, touch, keyboard flows), token proposals (hitSize, focusRing, previewElevation, nudgeStep), markup and CSS snippets, annotated interaction spec for engineers, accessibility checklist, and a small set of visual regression snapshots for the component test harness.

Acceptance criteria and test plan are in the acceptance_criteria field below.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard-only resize mode: Enter/Space to enter, Arrow keys to nudge, Shift+Arrow to jump, Escape to cancel, double-press auto-fit.
Mouse and touch drag show immediate ghost preview using transform and only commit to column width state at most every 200ms (debounced).
No full-table reflow or unmount during continuous drag in 10k-row virtualized scenario (verify with perf harness).
ARIA announcements for start/stop and width updates present in a polite live region and verified with screen reader testing notes.
Handles respect density tokens: cannot resize below minWidth token for active density; tooltip explains compression when reached.
Design tokens proposed and documented: hitSize, focusRing-4, previewElevation-1, nudgeStep-small, nudgeStep-large, resizeSnapThreshold.
Unit and e2e tests covering keyboard nudges, double-auto-fit, touch long-press entry, and a11y attributes present in DOM.
Design review approval from Accessibility and Component-API squads and an ENG implementation plan (ENG-18822 assigned).
comments: 2026-02-16 - Discovery: did quick lab test with existing grip; issues: 12px hit target, focus styling inconsistent, virtualization causes header jitter during drag.
2026-02-19 - UX research: 6 participants; keyboard-first flow was preferred by power users; touch long-press to enter resize worked best on mobile. Added nudge step and large jump behavior.

2026-02-24 - Engineering sync: discussed virtualization constraints with @Alex Nguyen (ENG). Agreed on preview overlay + debounced commit. ENG requested explicit perf budget: 100ms visible latency for preview updates, commits <= 200ms.

2026-03-02 - Accessibility review: @Priya Kapoor flagged the need for both live-region updates and alternate control buttons for SR users. Also requested a clear focus target > 8px and color token contrast >= 4.5:1.

2026-03-05 - Prototype: interactive Figma and a lightweight HTML prototype created. Link in related_links. Observed edge case: double-click auto-fit collides with column sort double-click; propose using Alt+double-click for auto-fit when header is sortable.

2026-03-09 - Design handoff draft posted. Waiting on ENG-20433 for updated table virtualization API (batch width updates). Next: finalize token names and ship spec to ENG with mockups and acceptance tests.
